title: Minimax Regret of Threshold Policy Learning under Coupled Effect and Propensity Tails
banked_reason: D0.5.G effective tier subfield below field floor: paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4, salvageable=false; known-logging rule-class and predecessor-positioning defects repaired in D0 graph 29aee8b9 after the cold review.
gap_reasons: Its asserted value for the Jin–Ren–Yang–Wang workflow remains prospective and unsupported by an implementation or substantive application.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a log-free n^-1/2 minimax rate for the declared global coupled-tail threshold class and a separate fixed-overlap n^-2/3 rate. The cold D0.5 review capped the contribution at subfield because the software use remained prospective, below the standing field floor. After the halt, the known-logging rule-class defect and accepted-predecessor comparison were repaired in the versioned graph and independently audited; the cold tier review was not rerun.
tldr: Known logging alone does not stabilize threshold welfare scores when propensities approach zero. On the declared global coupled-tail class, the sorted whole-observation-deletion IPW selector with \(q_n=n^{-1/2}\) attains uniform expected regret \(O(n^{-1/2})\) without a logarithmic loss, and a same-class rare-arm construction gives the matching all-selector lower bound. The proof uses the now-established atom-safe ordered \(L^2\) maximal inequality. On the fixed strict-overlap restriction, trimming is inactive and the same selector is ordinary EWM; the exponent-one margin localization yields the sharper matched rate \(n^{-2/3}\), making precise the cost of weak overlap in the present model.
gap: Published weak-overlap policy guarantees use an optimal-policy overlap index, a classwise propensity floor, or general clipping errors; published threshold-regret limits assume bounded overlap and a continuous index. The accepted predecessor supplies only a one-sided \(n^{-4/7}\) near-tie converse on a different truncated class.
fill: The project derives an atom-safe localized \(L^2\) chain maximum, a measurable \(O(n\log n)\) sorted trimmed-IPW selector, a log-free root-sample expected-regret upper bound, and a fixed-effect same-class Le Cam lower bound for every measurable selector.
